headline: Britain's AI minister will tell companies building the most advanced AI to do more on safety and say the country cannot rely entirely on them to police themselves, as he announces stronger cyber defences.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a government signal on AI safety and cyber defence, but it previews a speech and gives no detail of the new measures.
importance_line: UK residents, businesses and AI companies could face tougher expectations and stronger cyber protection, but the Guardian gives no detail of the new defences, and the speech will be watched for whether the UK joins an international call for common safety standards that neither the UK nor the US has signed.
summary: The Guardian reports that Kanishka Narayan, the UK's AI minister, will say in a speech in west London that companies building the most advanced AI should do more on safety, that Britain cannot rely entirely on technology firms to police their own models and that the UK needs more AI infrastructure of its own, as he announces a strengthening of the country's cyber defences. The paper adds that Geoffrey Irving, who used to be chief scientist at the UK's AI Security Institute (the government body that tests the most powerful AI models), told it: "The AI companies do not have security that would prevent an adversarial country from stealing the models"; OpenAI says it has protections including encryption and continuous monitoring.
notes: Read in full on The Guardian. The report previews a speech, so the wording is 'will say'; the cyber-defence measures are not described in the article.
